ko.title: [물류학 개론 #12] 여러분이 소유한 거의 모든 것을 옮기는 40피트 상자

segments.src: > International logistics is the business of moving goods across borders — mostly by ocean (cheap and slow), sometimes by air (fast and expensive), almost always inside a standardized container, and usually arranged by a middleman called a freight forwarder.
segments.tr: > 국제 물류는 국경을 넘어 상품을 이동시키는 비즈니스입니다. 주로 해상으로(저렴하고 느림), 때로는 항공으로(빠르고 비쌈), 거의 항상 표준화된 컨테이너 안에서 이루어지며, 대개 포워더(freight forwarder)라는 중개인이 주선합니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Look around the room you're in.
segments.tr: 당신이 있는 방 안을 둘러보세요.

segments.src: The laptop, the coffee mug, the sneakers by the door, the lithium cells in your earbuds — odds are most of it crossed an ocean before it reached you.
segments.tr: 노트북, 커피 머그잔, 문 앞의 운동화, 이어버드의 리튬 배터리까지 — 대부분 당신에게 닿기 전에 바다를 건너왔을 가능성이 높습니다.

segments.src: The question international logistics answers is deceptively simple: **how do you get a thing made in one country into the hands of someone in another, at a cost that still leaves room for profit?**
segments.tr: 국제 물류가 답하는 질문은 겉보기엔 단순합니다. **한 국가에서 만든 물건을, 이윤을 남길 수 있는 비용으로 다른 국가에 있는 사람의 손에 어떻게 쥐어줄 것인가?**

segments.src: Four pieces do most of the work.
segments.tr: 네 가지 요소가 대부분의 역할을 담당합니다.

segments.src: **Ocean freight** is the backbone.
segments.tr: **해상 운송**은 중추입니다.

segments.src: Roughly 80% of world merchandise trade by volume travels by sea, because ships are absurdly efficient per ton-mile.
segments.tr: 부피 기준으로 전 세계 상품 무역의 약 80%가 해상으로 이동하는데, 이는 선박이 톤-마일당 터무니없이 효율적이기 때문입니다.

segments.src: The tradeoff is time: Shanghai to Los Angeles runs about 14–18 days on the water, and Shanghai to New York (via Panama) closer to 30.
segments.tr: 트레이드오프는 시간입니다. 상하이에서 로스앤젤레스까지 해상으로 약 14~18일이 걸리고, 상하이에서 뉴욕(파나마 경유)까지는 약 30일이 걸립니다.

segments.src: Add port handling, customs, and inland trucking, and a realistic door-to-door number is often 30–45 days.
segments.tr: 항만 하역, 통관, 내륙 트럭 운송을 더하면 현실적인 문앞까지의 배송 기간은 보통 30~45일입니다.

segments.src: **Air freight** flips the equation.
segments.tr: **항공 운송**은 이 방정식을 뒤집습니다.

segments.src: Los Angeles to Frankfurt in a day or two, but at a cost that's commonly 10–20x ocean on a per-kilogram basis.
segments.tr: 로스앤젤레스에서 프랑크푸르트까지 하루 이틀이면 가지만, 비용은 킬로그램당 해상 운송의 보통 10~20배에 달합니다.

segments.src: So air gets reserved for goods where speed pays for itself: pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, fresh flowers, emergency spare parts, and the fashion item that has to hit stores before the season turns.
segments.tr: 따라서 항공은 속도가 비용을 상쇄하는 상품을 위해 남겨집니다. 의약품, 반도체, 신선한 꽃, 긴급 예비 부품, 그리고 시즌이 바뀌기 전에 매장에 들어가야 하는 패션 아이템 등이 그렇습니다.

segments.src: Only a small slice of trade by weight moves by air — but it's a much larger slice by *value*.
segments.tr: 중량 기준으로 무역에서 항공이 차지하는 비중은 작지만, *가치* 기준으로는 훨씬 더 큽니다.

segments.src: **The container** is the quiet hero.
segments.tr: **컨테이너**는 조용한 영웅입니다.

segments.src: Before Malcom McLean's standardized steel box debuted in 1956, cargo was loaded piece by piece by longshoremen — slow, theft-prone, and expensive.
segments.tr: 말콤 맥클린의 표준화된 강철 박스가 1956년에 데뷔하기 전에는 화물이 부두 노동자들에 의해 조각조각 선적되었습니다. 느리고, 도난에 취약하며, 비쌌습니다.

segments.src: Today the standard units are the **20-foot** and **40-foot** container, and industry volumes are counted in **TEU** (twenty-foot equivalent unit; one 40-footer = 2 TEU).
segments.tr: 오늘날 표준 단위는 **20피트**와 **40피트** 컨테이너이며, 업계 물동량은 **TEU**(twenty-foot equivalent unit; 40피트 컨테이너 1개 = 2 TEU)로 집계됩니다.

segments.src: The box's real magic is that it's *intermodal*: the same sealed unit moves from factory to truck to ship to rail to warehouse without anyone opening it.
segments.tr: 이 박스의 진짜 마법은 *인터모달(intermodal)*이라는 점입니다. 동일한 밀봉 단위가 아무도 열어보지 않은 채 공장에서 트럭, 선박, 철도, 창고로 이동합니다.

segments.src: That interchangeability is why a shirt can cross the Pacific for a few cents.
segments.tr: 이러한 호환성 덕분에 셔츠 한 벌이 몇 센트의 비용으로 태평양을 건널 수 있습니다.

segments.src: You'll also hear **FCL** (full container load — you rent the whole box) versus **LCL** (less than container load — your pallets share a box with other shippers' cargo).
segments.tr: 또한 **FCL**(full container load — 전체 박스를 대여)과 **LCL**(less than container load — 화물이 다른 화주들의 화물과 박스를 공유)에 대해서도 듣게 될 것입니다.

segments.src: FCL is cheaper per unit if you can fill it; LCL is how smaller businesses get in the game.
segments.tr: 채울 수만 있다면 FCL이 단위당 더 저렴하고, LCL은 소규모 기업들이 시장에 진입하는 방식입니다.

segments.src: **The freight forwarder** is who ties it together.
segments.tr: **포워더**는 이 모든 것을 하나로 묶는 주체입니다.

segments.src: A forwarder doesn't usually own ships or planes.
segments.tr: 포워더는 대개 선박이나 항공기를 소유하지 않습니다.

segments.src: It books space, consolidates smaller shipments, prepares the paperwork, arranges customs clearance, and manages the handoffs.
segments.tr: 공간을 예약하고, 소량 화물을 통합하고, 서류를 준비하고, 통관을 주선하고, 인수인계를 관리합니다.

segments.src: Think of it as a travel agent for cargo — except the itinerary involves customs bonds, a bill of lading, and a truck driver in New Jersey.
segments.tr: 화물을 위한 여행사라고 생각하면 됩니다. 다만 여정에 관세 보증서, 선하증권(bill of lading), 뉴저지의 트럭 운전사가 포함된다는 점이 다릅니다.

segments.src: One more concept worth knowing: **Incoterms**, the standardized three-letter trade terms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, and others) published by the International Chamber of Commerce.
segments.tr: 알아두어야 할 또 하나의 개념은 **인코텀즈(Incoterms)**입니다. 국제상업회의소(ICC)에서 발행한 표준화된 3글자 무역 조건(EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP 등)입니다.

segments.src: They define exactly where the seller's responsibility ends and the buyer's begins — who pays the freight, who carries the risk if the box goes overboard.
segments.tr: 이들은 판매자의 책임이 끝나고 구매자의 책임이 시작되는 지점을 정확히 정의합니다. 누가 운임을 지불하는지, 컨테이너가 바다에 빠질 경우 누가 리스크를 부담하는지 등을 말합니다.

segments.src: "FOB Shanghai" isn't jargon for its own sake; it's a precise allocation of cost and risk, and misreading it is how importers get surprise bills.
segments.tr: "FOB 상하이"는 그저 멋을 부린 전문 용어가 아닙니다. 비용과 리스크의 정확한 할당이며, 이를 오해하면 수입가들이 뜻밖의 청구서를 받게 됩니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 생활 속에서

segments.src: You order a $45 pair of running shoes online from a U.S.
segments.tr: 온라인에서 미국의 한 소매업체로부터 45달러짜리 러닝화 한 켤레를 주문합니다.

segments.src: retailer.
segments.tr: 소매업체.

segments.src: Here's the journey behind that price tag.
segments.tr: 그 가격표 뒤에 숨겨진 여정은 다음과 같습니다.

segments.src: The shoes are made in Vietnam.
segments.tr: 신발은 베트남에서 만들어집니다.

segments.src: The retailer's freight forwarder books space on a vessel out of Ho Chi Minh City.
segments.tr: 소매업체의 포워더는 호치민시를 출발하는 선박의 선적 공간을 예약합니다.

segments.src: The shoes — along with about 6,000 other pairs — go into a single 40-foot container, which the retailer has filled as FCL.
segments.tr: 신발은 약 6,000켤레의 다른 신발과 함께 단 하나의 40피트 컨테이너에 들어가며, 소매업체는 이를 FCL로 채웠습니다.

segments.src: That box crosses the Pacific in roughly two to three weeks and is craned off at the Port of Los Angeles or Long Beach, which together handle the largest container volumes in the United States.
segments.tr: 그 박스는 약 2~3주에 걸쳐 태평양을 건너 로스앤젤레스항이나 롱비치항에 하역됩니다. 이 두 항구는 미국에서 가장 큰 컨테이너 물동량을 공동으로 처리합니다.

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: **the ocean leg is often one of the cheapest lines on the invoice.** Trans-Pacific container rates swing wildly with market conditions — they spiked to extraordinary levels during the 2021 supply chain crunch and fell hard afterward — but spread across thousands of pairs, the per-shoe ocean cost typically lands in the range of pennies to a couple of dollars.
segments.tr: 사람들을 놀라게 하는 부분은 다음과 같습니다. **해상 운송 구간은 인보이스에서 가장 저렴한 항목 중 하나인 경우가 많습니다.** 태평양 횡단 컨테이너 운임은 시장 상황에 따라 극심하게 요동칩니다 — 2021년 공급망 대란 때 엄청난 수준으로 치솟았다가 그 후 급락했습니다 — 하지만 수천 켤레에 분산되면 신발 한 켤레당 해상 운송 비용은 대개 몇 센트에서 몇 달러 범위에 착지합니다.

segments.src: What costs real money afterward is everything on land: the drayage truck from the terminal to a warehouse in the Inland Empire, the customs duty (footwear tariff rates in the U.S.
segments.tr: 그 이후에 진짜 돈이 드는 것은 육상의 모든 것들입니다. 터미널에서 인랜드 엠파이어의 창고로 향하는 드레이리지(drayage) 트럭, 관세(미국의 신발 관세율은 특히 높습니다 — 많은 범주가 10%를 훨씬 웃돌고, 일부는 그 이상입니다), 분류 및 보관, 그리고 마지막으로 당신의 문 앞에 도착하는 라스트마일 배송 밴입니다.

segments.src: are notably high — many categories run well above 10%, some considerably more), the sorting and storage, and finally the last-mile delivery van that pulls up to your door.
segments.tr: 마지막 마일 — 교외 지역을 주행하는 몇 마일 — 은 그에 앞서 거쳐 온 7,000마일의 바다보다 더 많은 비용이 들 수 있습니다.

segments.src: That final mile — a few miles of suburban driving — can cost more than the 7,000 miles of ocean that preceded it.
segments.tr: 소매업체가 수요를 오판하여 연휴 주말 *전에* 2,000켤레가 더 필요한 경우라면 어떻게 될까요?

segments.src: And if the retailer misjudged demand and needs 2,000 more pairs *before* the holiday weekend?
segments.tr: 그 물량들은 호치민시를 떠나 항공편으로 시카고나 루이빌로 향합니다 — 며칠 만에 도착하지만, 각 켤레의 마진 대부분을 조용히 갉아먹을 수 있는 운송 비용이 듭니다.

segments.src: Those go by air out of Ho Chi Minh City to Chicago or Louisville — arriving in days, at a freight cost that can quietly eat most of the margin on each pair.
segments.tr: 이것이 단 하나의 결정에 담긴 전체 원칙입니다. **속도, 비용, 그리고 리스크, 이 세 가지를 모두 얻는 경우는 거의 없습니다.**

segments.src: That's the whole discipline in one decision: **speed, cost, and risk, and you rarely get all three.**
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: 1. 해상 운송은 톤-마일당 저렴하기 때문에 부피 기준으로 세계 무역의 압도적 다수를 이동시키고; 항공 운송은 중량 기준으로는 작은 몫을 이동시키지만 가치 기준으로는 큰 몫을 이동시키며, 비용의 대략 10~20배를 지불하고 속도를 삽니다.

segments.src: 1. Ocean freight moves the overwhelming majority of world trade by volume because it's cheap per ton-mile; air freight moves a small share by weight but a large share by value, buying speed at roughly 10–20x the cost.
segments.tr: 2. 표준화된 컨테이너(TEU로 집계됨)는 하나의 밀봉된 박스가 포장마저 뜯기지 않은 채 트럭, 선박, 철도를 가로질러 이동할 수 있게 함으로써 글로벌 무역을 저렴하게 만들었습니다.

segments.src: 2. The standardized container (counted in TEU) made global trade cheap by letting one sealed box move across truck, ship, and rail without ever being unpacked.
segments.tr: 3. 포워더는 예약, 통합, 통관 등 전체 체인을 조율하며, 인코텀즈는 판매자의 리스크와 비용이 끝나고 구매자의 리스크와 비용이 시작되는 지점을 정확히 정의합니다.

segments.src: 3. Freight forwarders orchestrate the whole chain — booking, consolidating, clearing customs — while Incoterms define exactly where the seller's risk and cost end and the buyer's begin.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: - **FCL / LCL** — Full Container Load (전체 박스를 예약함) 대 Less than Container Load (화물이 다른 화주의 화물과 박스를 공유함).

segments.src: - **TEU (Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit)** — The standard counting unit for container volume; a 40-foot container equals 2 TEU.
segments.tr: - **Freight forwarder** — 화주의 대행으로 화물을 주선하고 조율하는 회사로, 대개 선박이나 항공기 자체를 소유하지는 않습니다.

segments.src: - **FCL / LCL** — Full Container Load (you book the entire box) versus Less than Container Load (your cargo shares a box with other shippers').
segments.tr: - **Incoterms** — ICC에서 발행한 3글자 무역 조건(EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP 등)으로, 비용과 리스크가 판매자에서 구매자로 이전되는 지점을 정의합니다.

segments.src: - **Freight forwarder** — A company that arranges and coordinates shipments on a shipper's behalf, usually without owning the vessels or aircraft itself.
segments.tr: - **Drayage** — 항만 또는 철도 터미널과 인근 창고 사이에서 컨테이너를 이동시키는 단거리 트럭 운송.

segments.src: - **Incoterms** — ICC-published three-letter trade terms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, etc.) that define where cost and risk transfer from seller to buyer.
segments.tr: - **Bill of lading** — 핵심 선적 서류: 화물 수령증, 운송 계약의 증거, 그리고 종종 소유권 증서의 역할을 합니다.

segments.src: - **Drayage** — Short-haul trucking that moves a container between a port or rail terminal and a nearby warehouse.
- **Bill of lading** — The core shipping document: receipt for the goods, evidence of the transport contract, and often a document of title.

segments.tr: TEU는 20피트 표준을 기준으로 측정되므로, 40피트 박스는 2개로 집계됩니다.

TEU is measured against the 20-foot standard, so a 40-foot box counts as two.

zh.title: [物流 101 #12] 搬运你几乎所有物品的40英尺箱子

segments.src: > International logistics is the business of moving goods across borders — mostly by ocean (cheap and slow), sometimes by air (fast and expensive), almost always inside a standardized container, and usually arranged by a middleman called a freight forwarder.
segments.tr: > 国际物流是跨国运送货物的业务——主要通过海运（便宜且慢），有时通过空运（快且贵），几乎总是装在标准集装箱内，通常由名为货运代理的中介机构安排。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Look around the room you're in.
segments.tr: 看看你所在的房间。

segments.src: The laptop, the coffee mug, the sneakers by the door, the lithium cells in your earbuds — odds are most of it crossed an ocean before it reached you.
segments.tr: 笔记本电脑、咖啡杯、门边的运动鞋、耳机里的锂电池——大概率其中大部分在到达你手中之前都横跨了海洋。

segments.src: The question international logistics answers is deceptively simple: **how do you get a thing made in one country into the hands of someone in another, at a cost that still leaves room for profit?**
segments.tr: 国际物流所回答的问题看似简单：**如何将一个在一个国家制造的物品送到另一个国家的人手中，同时成本仍留有利润空间？**

segments.src: Four pieces do most of the work.
segments.tr: 四个部分完成了大部分工作。

segments.src: **Ocean freight** is the backbone.
segments.tr: **海运**是基石。

segments.src: Roughly 80% of world merchandise trade by volume travels by sea, because ships are absurdly efficient per ton-mile.
segments.tr: 按体积计算，全球约80%的商品贸易通过海运运输，因为船舶按吨英里计算效率高得惊人。

segments.src: The tradeoff is time: Shanghai to Los Angeles runs about 14–18 days on the water, and Shanghai to New York (via Panama) closer to 30.
segments.tr: 代价是时间：上海到洛杉矶在海上大约需要14–18天，而上海到纽约（经巴拿马）接近30天。

segments.src: Add port handling, customs, and inland trucking, and a realistic door-to-door number is often 30–45 days.
segments.tr: 加上港口处理、海关和内陆卡车运输，实际的门到门时间通常为30–45天。

segments.src: **Air freight** flips the equation.
segments.tr: **空运**颠覆了这个公式。

segments.src: Los Angeles to Frankfurt in a day or two, but at a cost that's commonly 10–20x ocean on a per-kilogram basis.
segments.tr: 洛杉矶到法兰克福只需一两天，但按每公斤计算，其成本通常是海运的10–20倍。

segments.src: So air gets reserved for goods where speed pays for itself: pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, fresh flowers, emergency spare parts, and the fashion item that has to hit stores before the season turns.
segments.tr: 因此，空运保留给速度物有所值的货物：药品、半导体、鲜花、紧急备件，以及必须在季节转换前上架的时尚单品。

segments.src: Only a small slice of trade by weight moves by air — but it's a much larger slice by *value*.
segments.tr: 按重量计算，一小部分贸易通过空运运输——但按*价值*计算，它占据了很大一部分。

segments.src: **The container** is the quiet hero.
segments.tr: **集装箱**是无声的英雄。

segments.src: Before Malcom McLean's standardized steel box debuted in 1956, cargo was loaded piece by piece by longshoremen — slow, theft-prone, and expensive.
segments.tr: 在马尔科姆·麦克莱恩（Malcom McLean）的标准化钢箱于1956年问世之前，货物是由码头工人一件一件装卸的——缓慢、易被盗且昂贵。

segments.src: Today the standard units are the **20-foot** and **40-foot** container, and industry volumes are counted in **TEU** (twenty-foot equivalent unit; one 40-footer = 2 TEU).
segments.tr: 如今，标准单位是**20英尺**和**40英尺**集装箱，行业吞吐量以**TEU**（二十英尺标准箱；一个40英尺集装箱 = 2 TEU）计算。

segments.src: The box's real magic is that it's *intermodal*: the same sealed unit moves from factory to truck to ship to rail to warehouse without anyone opening it.
segments.tr: 该箱子的真正魔力在于它是*多式联运*的：同一个密封单元从工厂移动到卡车、船舶、铁路再到仓库，无需任何人打开它。

segments.src: That interchangeability is why a shirt can cross the Pacific for a few cents.
segments.tr: 这种互换性正是衬衫能够以几美分跨越太平洋的原因。

segments.src: You'll also hear **FCL** (full container load — you rent the whole box) versus **LCL** (less than container load — your pallets share a box with other shippers' cargo).
segments.tr: 你还会听到**FCL**（整箱货——你租下整个箱子）与**LCL**（拼箱货——你的托盘与其它货主的货物共用一个箱子）。

segments.src: FCL is cheaper per unit if you can fill it; LCL is how smaller businesses get in the game.
segments.tr: 如果你能装满，FCL按单位计算更便宜；LCL则是小型企业进入该行业的方式。

segments.src: **The freight forwarder** is who ties it together.
segments.tr: **货运代理**是将这一切联系在一起的人。

segments.src: A forwarder doesn't usually own ships or planes.
segments.tr: 货运代理通常不拥有船舶或飞机。

segments.src: It books space, consolidates smaller shipments, prepares the paperwork, arranges customs clearance, and manages the handoffs.
segments.tr: 它预订舱位、拼装较小的货物、准备单证、安排清关并管理交接。

segments.src: Think of it as a travel agent for cargo — except the itinerary involves customs bonds, a bill of lading, and a truck driver in New Jersey.
segments.tr: 可以把它想象成货物的旅行社——除了行程涉及海关保证金、提单和新泽西州的卡车司机。

segments.src: One more concept worth knowing: **Incoterms**, the standardized three-letter trade terms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, and others) published by the International Chamber of Commerce.
segments.tr: 还有一个值得了解的概念：**Incoterms**（贸易术语），由国际商会发布的标准化三字母贸易条款（EXW、FOB、CIF、DDP等）。

segments.src: They define exactly where the seller's responsibility ends and the buyer's begins — who pays the freight, who carries the risk if the box goes overboard.
segments.tr: 它们确切地定义了卖方责任在哪里结束、买方责任在哪里开始——谁支付运费，如果箱子落水谁承担风险。

segments.src: "FOB Shanghai" isn't jargon for its own sake; it's a precise allocation of cost and risk, and misreading it is how importers get surprise bills.
segments.tr: "FOB Shanghai"不是为了说行话而说行话；它是对成本和风险的精确分配，误读它会导致进口商收到意料之外的账单。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 在日常生活中

segments.src: You order a $45 pair of running shoes online from a U.S.
segments.tr: 你在网上从美国零售商那里订购了一双售价45美元的跑鞋。

segments.src: retailer.
segments.tr: 零售商。

segments.src: Here's the journey behind that price tag.
segments.tr: 以下是该价格标签背后的历程。

segments.src: The shoes are made in Vietnam.
segments.tr: 鞋子产自越南。

segments.src: The retailer's freight forwarder books space on a vessel out of Ho Chi Minh City.
segments.tr: 零售商的货运代理在胡志明市出发的船只上预订了舱位。

segments.src: The shoes — along with about 6,000 other pairs — go into a single 40-foot container, which the retailer has filled as FCL.
segments.tr: 这些鞋子——连同大约6000双其他鞋子——装进了一个40英尺的集装箱中，零售商将其作为FCL整箱装载。

segments.src: That box crosses the Pacific in roughly two to three weeks and is craned off at the Port of Los Angeles or Long Beach, which together handle the largest container volumes in the United States.
segments.tr: 该箱子在大约两到三周内横跨太平洋，并在洛杉矶港或长滩港（它们共同处理美国最大的集装箱吞吐量）被起重机吊下。

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: **the ocean leg is often one of the cheapest lines on the invoice.** Trans-Pacific container rates swing wildly with market conditions — they spiked to extraordinary levels during the 2021 supply chain crunch and fell hard afterward — but spread across thousands of pairs, the per-shoe ocean cost typically lands in the range of pennies to a couple of dollars.
segments.tr: 让人吃惊的部分是：**海运航段通常是发票上最便宜的几行之一。** 跨太平洋集装箱运费随市场情况大幅波动——它们在2021年供应链危机期间飙升至非同寻常的水平，随后大幅下跌——但分摊到数千双鞋子时，每双鞋的海运成本通常在几美分到几美元之间。

segments.src: What costs real money afterward is everything on land: the drayage truck from the terminal to a warehouse in the Inland Empire, the customs duty (footwear tariff rates in the U.S.
segments.tr: 之后真正花钱的是陆地上的所有东西：从码头到内陆帝国仓库的短驳卡车、关税（美国的鞋类关税税率明显很高——许多类别远超10%，有些甚至更高）、分拣和仓储，以及最后驶向你家门口的最后一英里配送货车。

segments.src: are notably high — many categories run well above 10%, some considerably more), the sorting and storage, and finally the last-mile delivery van that pulls up to your door.
segments.tr: 最后这一英里——几英里的郊区驾驶——的花费可能会超过之前7000英里的海运。

segments.src: That final mile — a few miles of suburban driving — can cost more than the 7,000 miles of ocean that preceded it.
segments.tr: 这最后几英里——郊区驾驶的几英里——可能比之前的7000英里海运还要贵。

segments.src: And if the retailer misjudged demand and needs 2,000 more pairs *before* the holiday weekend?
segments.tr: 如果零售商误判了需求，在假日周末*之前*需要2000双鞋子怎么办？

segments.src: Those go by air out of Ho Chi Minh City to Chicago or Louisville — arriving in days, at a freight cost that can quietly eat most of the margin on each pair.
segments.tr: 这些鞋子将从胡志明市空运至芝加哥或路易斯安那州——几天内即可到达，其运费可能会悄悄吃掉每双鞋的大部分利润。

segments.src: That's the whole discipline in one decision: **speed, cost, and risk, and you rarely get all three.**
segments.tr: 这就是一个决定中的全部准则：**速度、成本和风险，你很少能三者兼得。**

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. Ocean freight moves the overwhelming majority of world trade by volume because it's cheap per ton-mile; air freight moves a small share by weight but a large share by value, buying speed at roughly 10–20x the cost.
segments.tr: 1. 按体积计算，海运承担了绝大部分全球贸易，因为它的吨英里成本低；空运按重量计算占一小部分，但按价值计算占很大一部分，以大约10–20倍的成本换取速度。

segments.src: 2. The standardized container (counted in TEU) made global trade cheap by letting one sealed box move across truck, ship, and rail without ever being unpacked.
segments.tr: 2. 标准化集装箱（以TEU计算）使一个密封箱子能够在卡车、船舶和铁路之间移动而无需拆包，从而使全球贸易变得廉价。

segments.src: 3. Freight forwarders orchestrate the whole chain — booking, consolidating, clearing customs — while Incoterms define exactly where the seller's risk and cost end and the buyer's begin.
segments.tr: 3. 货运代理统筹整个链条——预订、拼箱、清关——而Incoterms则精确定义了卖方风险和成本在哪里结束、买方风险和成本在哪里开始。

segments.src: **Air freight** flips the equation.
segments.tr: **हवाई माल भाड़ा** समीकरण को पलट देता है।

segments.src: Los Angeles to Frankfurt in a day or two, but at a cost that's commonly 10–20x ocean on a per-kilogram basis.
segments.tr: लॉस एंजिल्स से फ्रैंकफर्ट एक या दो दिन में, लेकिन एक ऐसी कीमत पर जो प्रति किलोग्राम के आधार पर आमतौर पर महासागर का 10-20 गुना है।

segments.src: So air gets reserved for goods where speed pays for itself: pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, fresh flowers, emergency spare parts, and the fashion item that has to hit stores before the season turns.
segments.tr: इसलिए हवा उन वस्तुओं के लिए आरक्षित हो जाती है जहाँ गति अपने लिए भुगतान करती है: फार्मास्यूटिकल्स, सेमीकंडक्टर, ताजे फूल, आपातकालीन स्पेयर पार्ट्स, और फैशन आइटम जिसे सीजन बदलने से पहले स्टोर तक पहुँचना होता है।

segments.src: Only a small slice of trade by weight moves by air — but it's a much larger slice by *value*.
segments.tr: वजन के हिसाब से व्यापार का केवल एक छोटा सा हिस्सा हवा से चलता है — लेकिन *मूल्य* के हिसाब से यह एक बहुत बड़ा हिस्सा है।

segments.src: **The container** is the quiet hero.
segments.tr: **कंटेनर** चुपचाप नायक है।

segments.src: Before Malcom McLean's standardized steel box debuted in 1956, cargo was loaded piece by piece by longshoremen — slow, theft-prone, and expensive.
segments.tr: 1956 में मैल्कम मैक्लीन के मानकीकृत स्टील बॉक्स की शुरुआत से पहले, कार्गो को डॉक वर्कर्स द्वारा टुकड़ा-टुकड़ा करके लोड किया जाता था — धीमा, चोरी-प्रवण और महंगा।

segments.src: Today the standard units are the **20-foot** and **40-foot** container, and industry volumes are counted in **TEU** (twenty-foot equivalent unit; one 40-footer = 2 TEU).
segments.tr: आज मानक इकाइयाँ **20-फुट** और **40-फुट** कंटेनर हैं, और उद्योग की मात्रा की गणना **TEU** (ट्वेंटी-फुट इक्विवेलेंट यूनिट; एक 40-फ़ूटर = 2 TEU) में की जाती है।

segments.src: The box's real magic is that it's *intermodal*: the same sealed unit moves from factory to truck to ship to rail to warehouse without anyone opening it.
segments.tr: बक्से का असली जादू यह है कि यह *इंटरमोडल* है: वही सील यूनिट किसी को भी खोले बिना कारखाने से ट्रक से जहाज से रेल से गोदाम तक जाती है।

segments.src: That interchangeability is why a shirt can cross the Pacific for a few cents.
segments.tr: वह विनिमेयता यही कारण है कि एक शर्ट कुछ सेंट के लिए प्रशांत पार कर सकती है।

segments.src: You'll also hear **FCL** (full container load — you rent the whole box) versus **LCL** (less than container load — your pallets share a box with other shippers' cargo).
segments.tr: आप **FCL** (फुल कंटेनर लोड — आप पूरा बॉक्स किराए पर लेते हैं) बनाम **LCL** (कम से कम कंटेनर लोड — आपके pallets अन्य शिपर्स के कार्गो के साथ एक बॉक्स साझा करते हैं) भी सुनेंगे।

segments.src: FCL is cheaper per unit if you can fill it; LCL is how smaller businesses get in the game.
segments.tr: यदि आप इसे भर सकते हैं तो FCL प्रति यूनिट सस्ता है; LCL वह है जिससे छोटे व्यवसाय खेल में प्रवेश करते हैं।

segments.src: **The freight forwarder** is who ties it together.
segments.tr: **फ्रेट फ़ॉरवर्ड** वह है जो इसे एक साथ बांधता है।

segments.src: A forwarder doesn't usually own ships or planes.
segments.tr: एक फ़ॉरवर्ड आमतौर पर जहाजों या विमानों का मालिक नहीं होता है।

segments.src: It books space, consolidates smaller shipments, prepares the paperwork, arranges customs clearance, and manages the handoffs.
segments.tr: यह अंतरिक्ष बुक करता है, छोटे शिपमेंट को समेकित करता है, कागजी कार्रवाई तैयार करता है, सीमा शुल्क निकासी की व्यवस्था करता है, और हैंडऑफ़ का प्रबंधन करता है।

segments.src: Think of it as a travel agent for cargo — except the itinerary involves customs bonds, a bill of lading, and a truck driver in New Jersey.
segments.tr: इसे कार्गो के लिए एक ट्रैवल एजेंट के रूप में सोचें — सिवाय इसके कि यात्रा कार्यक्रम में कस्टम बॉन्ड, लाडिंग का बिल और न्यू जर्सी में एक ट्रक ड्राइवर शामिल है।

segments.src: One more concept worth knowing: **Incoterms**, the standardized three-letter trade terms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, and others) published by the International Chamber of Commerce.
segments.tr: जानने लायक एक और अवधारणा: **इन्कोटर्म्स**, अंतर्राष्ट्रीय चैंबर ऑफ कॉमर्स द्वारा प्रकाशित मानकीकृत तीन-अक्षर व्यापार शर्तें (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, और अन्य)।

segments.src: They define exactly where the seller's responsibility ends and the buyer's begins — who pays the freight, who carries the risk if the box goes overboard.
segments.tr: वे ठीक से परिभाषित करते हैं कि विक्रेता की जिम्मेदारी कहाँ समाप्त होती है और खरीदार की कहाँ शुरू होती है — कौन माल ढुलाई का भुगतान करता है, यदि बॉक्स ओवरबोर्ड जाता है तो जोखिम कौन उठाता है।

segments.src: "FOB Shanghai" isn't jargon for its own sake; it's a precise allocation of cost and risk, and misreading it is how importers get surprise bills.
segments.tr: "FOB शंघाई" अपने आप में शब्दजाल नहीं है; यह लागत और जोखिम का एक सटीक आवंटन है, और इसे गलत पढ़ना यह है कि आयातकों को आश्चर्यजनक बिल कैसे मिलते हैं।

segments.tr: ## दैनिक जीवन में

segments.src: You order a $45 pair of running shoes online from a U.S.

segments.tr: जूते — लगभग 6,000 अन्य जोड़ों के साथ — एक एकल 40-फुट कंटेनर में जाते हैं, जिसे खुदरा विक्रेता ने FCL के रूप में भरा है।

segments.src: That box crosses the Pacific in roughly two to three weeks and is craned off at the Port of Los Angeles or Long Beach, which together handle the largest container volumes in the United States.
segments.tr: वह बॉक्स लगभग दो से तीन सप्ताह में प्रशांत पार करता है और लॉस एंजिल्स या लॉन्ग बीच के बंदरगाह पर क्रेन से उतार दिया जाता है, जो संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका में सबसे बड़े कंटेनर वॉल्यूम को संभालते हैं।

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: **the ocean leg is often one of the cheapest lines on the invoice.** Trans-Pacific container rates swing wildly with market conditions — they spiked to extraordinary levels during the 2021 supply chain crunch and fell hard afterward — but spread across thousands of pairs, the per-shoe ocean cost typically lands in the range of pennies to a couple of dollars.
segments.tr: यहाँ वह हिस्सा है जो लोगों को आश्चर्यचकित करता है: **महासागरीय पैर अक्सर चालान पर सबसे सस्ती लाइनों में से एक है।** ट्रांस-पैसिफिक कंटेनर दरें बाजार की स्थिति के साथ तेजी से उतार-चढ़ाव करती हैं — वे 2021 की आपूर्ति श्रृंखला संकट के दौरान असाधारण स्तर पर बढ़ गईं और बाद में जोर से गिर गईं — लेकिन हजारों जोड़े में फैल गईं, प्रति-जूते महासागर लागत आमतौर पर pennies से लेकर कुछ डॉलर की सीमा में उतरती है।

segments.tr: विशेष रूप से उच्च हैं — कई श्रेणियां 10% से काफी ऊपर चलती हैं, कुछ काफी अधिक), छँटाई और भंडारण, और अंत में अंतिम मील डिलीवरी वैन जो आपके दरवाजे पर खींचती है।

segments.src: That final mile — a few miles of suburban driving — can cost more than the 7,000 miles of ocean that preceded it.
segments.tr: वह अंतिम मील — उपनगरीय ड्राइविंग के कुछ मील — इसके पहले आने वाले समुद्र के 7,000 मील की तुलना में अधिक खर्च कर सकता है।

segments.src: And if the retailer misjudged demand and needs 2,000 more pairs *before* the holiday weekend?
segments.tr: और अगर खुदरा विक्रेता ने मांग का गलत अनुमान लगाया और छुट्टी सप्ताहांत *से पहले* 2,000 और जोड़े की आवश्यकता है?

segments.src: Those go by air out of Ho Chi Minh City to Chicago or Louisville — arriving in days, at a freight cost that can quietly eat most of the margin on each pair.
segments.tr: वे हो ची मिह सिटी से शिकागो या लुइसविले के लिए हवा से बाहर जाते हैं — दिनों में पहुंचते हैं, एक माल ढुलाई लागत पर जो चुपचाप प्रत्येक जोड़ी पर अधिकांश मार्जिन खा सकती है।

segments.src: That's the whole discipline in one decision: **speed, cost, and risk, and you rarely get all three.**
segments.tr: यह एक निर्णय में पूरा अनुशासन है: **गति, लागत और जोखिम, और आपको शायद ही कभी तीनों मिलते हैं।**

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति सारांश

segments.src: 1. Ocean freight moves the overwhelming majority of world trade by volume because it's cheap per ton-mile; air freight moves a small share by weight but a large share by value, buying speed at roughly 10–20x the cost.
segments.tr: 1. महासागरीय माल भाड़ा मात्रा के हिसाब से विश्व व्यापार के भारी बहुमत को स्थानांतरित करता है क्योंकि यह टन-मील प्रति सस्ता है; हवाई माल भाड़ा वजन द्वारा एक छोटा हिस्सा स्थानांतरित करता है लेकिन मूल्य द्वारा एक बड़ा हिस्सा, लगभग 10-20 गुना लागत पर गति खरीदता है।

segments.src: 2. The standardized container (counted in TEU) made global trade cheap by letting one sealed box move across truck, ship, and rail without ever being unpacked.
segments.tr: 2. मानकीकृत कंटेनर (TEU में गिना जाता है) ने वैश्विक व्यापार को एक सील बॉक्स को बिना खोले ट्रक, जहाज और रेल में ले जाने की अनुमति देकर सस्ता बना दिया।

segments.src: 3. Freight forwarders orchestrate the whole chain — booking, consolidating, clearing customs — while Incoterms define exactly where the seller's risk and cost end and the buyer's begin.
segments.tr: 3. फ्रेट फ़ॉरवर्ड पूरी श्रृंखला को ऑर्केस्ट्रेट करते हैं — बुकिंग, समेकन, सीमा शुल्क निकासी — जबकि इन्कोटर्म्स यह परिभाषित करते हैं कि विक्रेता का जोखिम और लागत कहाँ समाप्त होती है और खरीदार की कहाँ शुरू होती है।

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज की शर्तें

segments.src: - **TEU (Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit)** — The standard counting unit for container volume; a 40-foot container equals 2 TEU.
segments.tr: - **TEU (Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit)** — कंटेनर वॉल्यूम के लिए मानक गिनती इकाई; एक 40-फुट कंटेनर 2 TEU के बराबर है।

segments.src: - **FCL / LCL** — Full Container Load (you book the entire box) versus Less than Container Load (your cargo shares a box with other shippers').
segments.tr: - **FCL / LCL** — फुल कंटेनर लोड (आप पूरा बॉक्स बुक करते हैं) बनाम लेस दैन कंटेनर लोड (आपका कार्गो अन्य शिपर्स के साथ एक बॉक्स साझा करता है)।

segments.src: - **Freight forwarder** — A company that arranges and coordinates shipments on a shipper's behalf, usually without owning the vessels or aircraft itself.
segments.tr: - **Freight forwarder** — एक कंपनी जो एक शिपर की ओर से शिपमेंट की व्यवस्था और समन्वय करती है, आमतौर पर जहाजों या विमानों को खुद के बिना।

segments.src: - **Incoterms** — ICC-published three-letter trade terms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, etc.) that define where cost and risk transfer from seller to buyer.
segments.tr: - **Incoterms** — ICC-प्रकाशित तीन-अक्षर व्यापार शर्तें (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, आदि) जो परिभाषित करती हैं कि लागत और जोखिम विक्रेता से खरीदार को कहाँ स्थानांतरित होते हैं।

segments.src: - **Drayage** — Short-haul trucking that moves a container between a port or rail terminal and a nearby warehouse.
segments.tr: - **Drayage** — शॉर्ट-हॉल ट्रकिंग जो एक बंदरगाह या रेल टर्मिनल और एक नजदीकी गोदाम के बीच एक कंटेनर को स्थानांतरित करती है।

segments.src: - **Bill of lading** — The core shipping document: receipt for the goods, evidence of the transport contract, and often a document of title.
segments.tr: - **Bill of lading** — मूल शिपिंग दस्तावेज़: माल के लिए रसीद, परिवहन अनुबंध का प्रमाण, और अक्सर शीर्षक का एक दस्तावेज।

es.title: [Logística 101 #12] La caja de 40 pies que mueve casi todo lo que posees

segments.src: > International logistics is the business of moving goods across borders — mostly by ocean (cheap and slow), sometimes by air (fast and expensive), almost always inside a standardized container, and usually arranged by a middleman called a freight forwarder.
segments.tr: > La logística internacional es el negocio de mover mercancías a través de las fronteras — principalmente por mar (barato y lento), a veces por aire (rápido y caro), casi siempre dentro de un contenedor estandarizado, y por lo general gestionado por un intermediario llamado transitario.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## El concepto de hoy

segments.src: Look around the room you're in.
segments.tr: Mira a tu alrededor en la habitación en la que estás.

segments.src: The laptop, the coffee mug, the sneakers by the door, the lithium cells in your earbuds — odds are most of it crossed an ocean before it reached you.
segments.tr: La laptop, la taza de café, los tenis junto a la puerta, las celdas de litio en tus audífonos — lo más probable es que la mayor parte haya cruzado un océano antes de llegar a ti.

segments.src: The question international logistics answers is deceptively simple: **how do you get a thing made in one country into the hands of someone in another, at a cost that still leaves room for profit?**
segments.tr: La pregunta que responde la logística internacional es engañosamente simple: **¿cómo haces que algo hecho en un país llegue a manos de alguien en otro, a un costo que aún deje margen para la ganancia?**

segments.src: Four pieces do most of the work.
segments.tr: Cuatro piezas hacen la mayor parte del trabajo.

segments.src: **Ocean freight** is the backbone.
segments.tr: **El transporte marítimo** es la columna vertebral.

segments.src: Roughly 80% of world merchandise trade by volume travels by sea, because ships are absurdly efficient per ton-mile.
segments.tr: Aproximadamente el 80% del comercio mundial de mercancías por volumen viaja por mar, porque los barcos son absurdamente eficientes por tonelada-milla.

segments.src: The tradeoff is time: Shanghai to Los Angeles runs about 14–18 days on the water, and Shanghai to New York (via Panama) closer to 30.
segments.tr: El inconveniente es el tiempo: Shanghái a Los Ángeles toma unos 14–18 días en el agua, y Shanghái a Nueva York (vía Panamá) se acerca a los 30.

segments.src: Add port handling, customs, and inland trucking, and a realistic door-to-door number is often 30–45 days.
segments.tr: Agrega el manejo portuario, aduanas y transporte terrestre por camión, y una cifra realista de puerta a puerta suele ser de 30–45 días.

segments.src: **Air freight** flips the equation.
segments.tr: **El transporte aéreo** invierte la ecuación.

segments.src: Los Angeles to Frankfurt in a day or two, but at a cost that's commonly 10–20x ocean on a per-kilogram basis.
segments.tr: De Los Ángeles a Fráncfort en uno o dos días, pero a un costo que comúnmente es de 10 a 20 veces el del mar por kilogramo.

segments.src: So air gets reserved for goods where speed pays for itself: pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, fresh flowers, emergency spare parts, and the fashion item that has to hit stores before the season turns.
segments.tr: Así que el aire se reserva para bienes donde la velocidad se paga por sí misma: productos farmacéuticos, semiconductores, flores frescas, repuestos de emergencia y el artículo de moda que tiene que llegar a las tiendas antes de que cambie la temporada.

segments.src: Only a small slice of trade by weight moves by air — but it's a much larger slice by *value*.
segments.tr: Solo una pequeña parte del comercio por peso se mueve por aire — pero es una parte mucho mayor por *valor*.

segments.src: **The container** is the quiet hero.
segments.tr: **El contenedor** es el héroe silencioso.

segments.src: Before Malcom McLean's standardized steel box debuted in 1956, cargo was loaded piece by piece by longshoremen — slow, theft-prone, and expensive.
segments.tr: Antes de que debutara la caja de acero estandarizada de Malcom McLean en 1956, la carga se cargaba pieza por pieza por estibadores — lento, propenso a robos y caro.

segments.src: Today the standard units are the **20-foot** and **40-foot** container, and industry volumes are counted in **TEU** (twenty-foot equivalent unit; one 40-footer = 2 TEU).
segments.tr: Hoy en día, las unidades estándar son el contenedor de **20 pies** y de **40 pies**, y los volúmenes de la industria se cuentan en **TEU** (unidad equivalente a veinte pies; un contenedor de 40 pies = 2 TEU).

segments.src: The box's real magic is that it's *intermodal*: the same sealed unit moves from factory to truck to ship to rail to warehouse without anyone opening it.
segments.tr: La verdadera magia de la caja es que es *intermodal*: la misma unidad sellada se mueve de la fábrica al camión, al barco, al tren y al almacén sin que nadie la abra.

segments.src: That interchangeability is why a shirt can cross the Pacific for a few cents.
segments.tr: Esa intercambiabilidad es la razón por la cual una camisa puede cruzar el Pacífico por unos pocos centavos.

segments.src: You'll also hear **FCL** (full container load — you rent the whole box) versus **LCL** (less than container load — your pallets share a box with other shippers' cargo).
segments.tr: También oirás hablar de **FCL** (carga de contenedor completo — alquilas toda la caja) frente a **LCL** (carga menor que un contenedor — tus palés comparten caja con la carga de otros expedidores).

segments.src: FCL is cheaper per unit if you can fill it; LCL is how smaller businesses get in the game.
segments.tr: FCL es más barato por unidad si puedes llenarlo; LCL es cómo las empresas más pequeñas entran en el juego.

segments.src: **The freight forwarder** is who ties it together.
segments.tr: **El transitario** es quien lo une todo.

segments.src: A forwarder doesn't usually own ships or planes.
segments.tr: Un transitario por lo general no posee barcos ni aviones.

segments.src: It books space, consolidates smaller shipments, prepares the paperwork, arranges customs clearance, and manages the handoffs.
segments.tr: Reserva espacio, consolida envíos más pequeños, prepara el papeleo, organiza el despacho de aduanas y gestiona las entregas.

segments.src: Think of it as a travel agent for cargo — except the itinerary involves customs bonds, a bill of lading, and a truck driver in New Jersey.
segments.tr: Piénsalo como una agencia de viajes para carga — excepto que el itinerario incluye bonos de aduana, un conocimiento de embarque y un camionero en Nueva Jersey.

segments.src: One more concept worth knowing: **Incoterms**, the standardized three-letter trade terms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, and others) published by the International Chamber of Commerce.
segments.tr: Un concepto más que vale la pena conocer: **Incoterms**, los términos comerciales estandarizados de tres letras (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP y otros) publicados por la Cámara de Comercio Internacional.

segments.src: They define exactly where the seller's responsibility ends and the buyer's begins — who pays the freight, who carries the risk if the box goes overboard.
segments.tr: Definen exactamente dónde termina la responsabilidad del vendedor y comienza la del comprador — quién paga el flete, quién asume el riesgo si la caja cae al agua.

segments.src: "FOB Shanghai" isn't jargon for its own sake; it's a precise allocation of cost and risk, and misreading it is how importers get surprise bills.
segments.tr: "FOB Shanghái" no es jerga por el simple hecho de serlo; es una asignación precisa de costo y riesgo, y malinterpretarla es la forma en que los importadores reciben facturas sorpresa.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: You order a $45 pair of running shoes online from a U.S.

segments.tr: UU.

segments.src: Here's the journey behind that price tag.
segments.tr: Este es el viaje detrás de esa etiqueta de precio.

segments.src: The shoes are made in Vietnam.
segments.tr: Los zapatos están hechos en Vietnam.

segments.src: The retailer's freight forwarder books space on a vessel out of Ho Chi Minh City.
segments.tr: El transitario del minorista reserva espacio en un buque que sale de Ciudad Ho Chi Minh.

segments.src: The shoes — along with about 6,000 other pairs — go into a single 40-foot container, which the retailer has filled as FCL.
segments.tr: Los zapatos — junto con otros 6,000 pares aproximadamente — van en un solo contenedor de 40 pies, que el minorista ha llenado como FCL.

segments.src: That box crosses the Pacific in roughly two to three weeks and is craned off at the Port of Los Angeles or Long Beach, which together handle the largest container volumes in the United States.

segments.tr: Lo que cuesta dinero real después es todo lo que está en tierra: el camión de acarreo desde la terminal hasta un almacén en el Inland Empire, el arancel de aduana (las tasas arancelarias para el calzado en EE.

segments.tr: UU. son notablemente altas — muchas categorías superan con creces el 10%, algunas considerablemente más), la clasificación y el almacenamiento, y finalmente la camioneta de entrega de última milla que se detiene en tu puerta.

segments.src: That final mile — a few miles of suburban driving — can cost more than the 7,000 miles of ocean that preceded it.
segments.tr: Esa última milla — unas pocas millas de manejo suburbano — puede costar más que las 7,000 millas de océano que la precedieron.

segments.src: And if the retailer misjudged demand and needs 2,000 more pairs *before* the holiday weekend?
segments.tr: Y si el minorista calcula mal la demanda y necesita 2,000 pares más *antes* del fin de semana festivo?

segments.src: Those go by air out of Ho Chi Minh City to Chicago or Louisville — arriving in days, at a freight cost that can quietly eat most of the margin on each pair.
segments.tr: Esos van por aire desde Ciudad Ho Chi Minh a Chicago o Louisville — llegando en días, a un costo de flete que puede consumir silenciosamente la mayor parte del margen de cada par.

segments.src: That's the whole discipline in one decision: **speed, cost, and risk, and you rarely get all three.**
segments.tr: Esa es toda la disciplina en una sola decisión: **velocidad, costo y riesgo, y rara vez se obtienen los tres.**

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumen de tres líneas

segments.src: 1. Ocean freight moves the overwhelming majority of world trade by volume because it's cheap per ton-mile; air freight moves a small share by weight but a large share by value, buying speed at roughly 10–20x the cost.
segments.tr: 1. El transporte marítimo mueve la abrumadora mayoría del comercio mundial por volumen porque es barato por tonelada-milla; el transporte aéreo mueve una pequeña parte por peso pero una gran parte por valor, comprando velocidad a aproximadamente 10–20x del costo.

segments.src: 2. The standardized container (counted in TEU) made global trade cheap by letting one sealed box move across truck, ship, and rail without ever being unpacked.
segments.tr: 2. El contenedor estandarizado (contado en TEU) abarató el comercio global al permitir que una caja sellada se moviera en camión, barco y tren sin ser desempacada.

segments.src: 3. Freight forwarders orchestrate the whole chain — booking, consolidating, clearing customs — while Incoterms define exactly where the seller's risk and cost end and the buyer's begin.
segments.tr: 3. Los transitarios orquestan toda la cadena — reservando, consolidando, pasando aduanas — mientras que los Incoterms definen exactamente dónde terminan el riesgo y el costo del vendedor y comienzan los del comprador.

fr.title: [Logistique 101 #12] La boîte de 40 pieds qui transporte presque tout ce que vous possédez

segments.src: > International logistics is the business of moving goods across borders — mostly by ocean (cheap and slow), sometimes by air (fast and expensive), almost always inside a standardized container, and usually arranged by a middleman called a freight forwarder.
segments.tr: > La logistique internationale est l'activité qui consiste à acheminer des marchandises au-delà des frontières — principalement par voie maritime (bon marché et lente), parfois par voie aérienne (rapide et coûteuse), presque toujours dans un conteneur standardisé, et généralement organisée par un intermédiaire appelé transitaire.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le concept du jour

segments.src: Look around the room you're in.
segments.tr: Regardez autour de vous dans la pièce où vous vous trouvez.

segments.src: The laptop, the coffee mug, the sneakers by the door, the lithium cells in your earbuds — odds are most of it crossed an ocean before it reached you.
segments.tr: L'ordinateur portable, la tasse de café, les baskets près de la porte, les cellules au lithium de vos écouteurs — il y a fort à parier qu'une grande partie a traversé un océan avant de vous parvenir.

segments.src: The question international logistics answers is deceptively simple: **how do you get a thing made in one country into the hands of someone in another, at a cost that still leaves room for profit?**
segments.tr: La question à laquelle répond la logistique internationale est faussement simple : **comment faire pour qu'un objet fabriqué dans un pays se retrouve entre les mains de quelqu'un dans un autre, à un coût qui laisse encore de la marge pour le profit ?**

segments.src: Four pieces do most of the work.
segments.tr: Quatre éléments font l'essentiel du travail.

segments.src: **Ocean freight** is the backbone.
segments.tr: **Le transport maritime** est l'épine dorsale.

segments.src: Roughly 80% of world merchandise trade by volume travels by sea, because ships are absurdly efficient per ton-mile.
segments.tr: Environ 80 % du commerce mondial de marchandises en volume voyage par mer, car les navires sont incroyablement efficaces par tonne-mille.

segments.src: The tradeoff is time: Shanghai to Los Angeles runs about 14–18 days on the water, and Shanghai to New York (via Panama) closer to 30.
segments.tr: Le compromis est le temps : Shanghai-Los Angeles prend environ 14 à 18 jours sur l'eau, et Shanghai-New York (via Panama) s'approche de 30.

segments.src: Add port handling, customs, and inland trucking, and a realistic door-to-door number is often 30–45 days.
segments.tr: Ajoutez la manutention portuaire, les douanes et le transport routier intérieur, et un chiffre réaliste de porte-à-porte est souvent de 30 à 45 jours.

segments.src: **Air freight** flips the equation.
segments.tr: **Le fret aérien** inverse l'équation.

segments.src: Los Angeles to Frankfurt in a day or two, but at a cost that's commonly 10–20x ocean on a per-kilogram basis.
segments.tr: Los Angeles-Francfort en un jour ou deux, mais à un coût qui représente généralement 10 à 20 fois celui de la mer sur une base par kilogramme.

segments.src: So air gets reserved for goods where speed pays for itself: pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, fresh flowers, emergency spare parts, and the fashion item that has to hit stores before the season turns.
segments.tr: L'avion est donc réservé aux marchandises où la vitesse se paie d'elle-même : produits pharmaceutiques, semi-conducteurs, fleurs fraîches, pièces de rechange d'urgence et articles de mode qui doivent arriver en magasin avant le changement de saison.

segments.src: Only a small slice of trade by weight moves by air — but it's a much larger slice by *value*.
segments.tr: Seule une petite partie du commerce en poids voyage par air — mais c'est une part beaucoup plus importante en *valeur*.

segments.src: **The container** is the quiet hero.
segments.tr: **Le conteneur** est le héros discret.

segments.src: Before Malcom McLean's standardized steel box debuted in 1956, cargo was loaded piece by piece by longshoremen — slow, theft-prone, and expensive.
segments.tr: Avant que la boîte en acier standardisée de Malcom McLean ne fasse ses débuts en 1956, la cargaison était chargée pièce par pièce par des dockers — lent, sujet au vol et cher.

segments.src: Today the standard units are the **20-foot** and **40-foot** container, and industry volumes are counted in **TEU** (twenty-foot equivalent unit; one 40-footer = 2 TEU).
segments.tr: Aujourd'hui, les unités standard sont le conteneur de **20 pieds** et de **40 pieds**, et les volumes de l'industrie sont comptés en **EVP** (équivalent vingt pieds ; un conteneur de 40 pieds = 2 EVP).

segments.src: The box's real magic is that it's *intermodal*: the same sealed unit moves from factory to truck to ship to rail to warehouse without anyone opening it.
segments.tr: La vraie magie de la boîte est qu'elle est *intermodale* : la même unité scellée passe de l'usine au camion, au navire, au train et à l'entrepôt sans que personne ne l'ouvre.

segments.src: That interchangeability is why a shirt can cross the Pacific for a few cents.
segments.tr: Cette interchangeabilité est la raison pour laquelle une chemise peut traverser le Pacifique pour quelques centimes.

segments.src: You'll also hear **FCL** (full container load — you rent the whole box) versus **LCL** (less than container load — your pallets share a box with other shippers' cargo).
segments.tr: Vous entendrez également parler de **FCL** (chargement complet de conteneur — vous louez toute la boîte) par rapport à **LCL** (chargement partiel de conteneur — vos palettes partagent une boîte avec la cargaison d'autres expéditeurs).

segments.src: FCL is cheaper per unit if you can fill it; LCL is how smaller businesses get in the game.
segments.tr: Le FCL est moins cher par unité si vous pouvez le remplir ; le LCL est la façon dont les petites entreprises entrent dans le jeu.

segments.src: **The freight forwarder** is who ties it together.
segments.tr: **Le transitaire** est celui qui lie le tout.

segments.src: A forwarder doesn't usually own ships or planes.
segments.tr: Un transitaire ne possède généralement ni navires ni avions.

segments.src: It books space, consolidates smaller shipments, prepares the paperwork, arranges customs clearance, and manages the handoffs.
segments.tr: Il réserve de l'espace, consolide les envois plus petits, prépare la paperasse, organise le dédouanement et gère les transferts.

segments.src: Think of it as a travel agent for cargo — except the itinerary involves customs bonds, a bill of lading, and a truck driver in New Jersey.
segments.tr: Considérez cela comme une agence de voyages pour le fret — sauf que l'itinéraire implique des cautions de douane, un connaissement et un chauffeur de camion dans le New Jersey.

segments.src: One more concept worth knowing: **Incoterms**, the standardized three-letter trade terms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, and others) published by the International Chamber of Commerce.
segments.tr: Encore un concept à connaître : **les Incoterms**, les termes commerciaux normalisés à trois lettres (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP et autres) publiés par la Chambre de commerce internationale.

segments.src: They define exactly where the seller's responsibility ends and the buyer's begins — who pays the freight, who carries the risk if the box goes overboard.
segments.tr: Ils définissent exactement où la responsabilité du vendeur se termine et où celle de l'acheteur commence — qui paie le fret, qui supporte le risque si la boîte passe par-dessus bord.

segments.src: "FOB Shanghai" isn't jargon for its own sake; it's a precise allocation of cost and risk, and misreading it is how importers get surprise bills.
segments.tr: "FOB Shanghai" n'est pas du jargon pour le plaisir ; c'est une allocation précise des coûts et des risques, et le mal interpréter est la façon dont les importateurs reçoivent des factures surprises.

segments.src: Add port handling, customs, and inland trucking, and a realistic door-to-door number is often 30–45 days.
segments.tr: Adicione manuseio portuário, alfândega e transporte rodoviário interno, e um número realista porta-a-porta é frequentemente de 30–45 dias.

segments.src: **Air freight** flips the equation.
segments.tr: **Frete aéreo** inverte a equação.

segments.src: Los Angeles to Frankfurt in a day or two, but at a cost that's commonly 10–20x ocean on a per-kilogram basis.
segments.tr: De Los Angeles a Frankfurt em um ou dois dias, mas a um custo que é comumente 10–20x o marítimo por quilograma.

segments.src: So air gets reserved for goods where speed pays for itself: pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, fresh flowers, emergency spare parts, and the fashion item that has to hit stores before the season turns.
segments.tr: Portanto, o aéreo é reservado para mercadorias onde a velocidade se paga: produtos farmacêuticos, semicondutores, flores frescas, peças de reposição de emergência e aquele item de moda que precisa chegar às lojas antes que a estação mude.

segments.src: Only a small slice of trade by weight moves by air — but it's a much larger slice by *value*.
segments.tr: Apenas uma pequena fatia do comércio por peso se move por via aérea — mas é uma fatia muito maior por *valor*.

segments.src: **The container** is the quiet hero.
segments.tr: **O contêiner** é o herói silencioso.

segments.src: Before Malcom McLean's standardized steel box debuted in 1956, cargo was loaded piece by piece by longshoremen — slow, theft-prone, and expensive.
segments.tr: Antes que a caixa de aço padronizada de Malcom McLean estreasse em 1956, a carga era carregada peça por peça por estivadores — lento, propenso a roubos e caro.

segments.src: Today the standard units are the **20-foot** and **40-foot** container, and industry volumes are counted in **TEU** (twenty-foot equivalent unit; one 40-footer = 2 TEU).
segments.tr: Hoje, as unidades padrão são o contêiner de **20 pés** e **40 pés**, e os volumes da indústria são contados em **TEU** (unidade equivalente a vinte pés; um de 40 pés = 2 TEU).

segments.src: The box's real magic is that it's *intermodal*: the same sealed unit moves from factory to truck to ship to rail to warehouse without anyone opening it.
segments.tr: A verdadeira mágica da caixa é que ela é *intermodal*: a mesma unidade selada se move da fábrica para o caminhão, para o navio, para o trem e para o armazém sem que ninguém a abra.

segments.src: That interchangeability is why a shirt can cross the Pacific for a few cents.
segments.tr: Essa intercambialidade é o motivo pelo qual uma camisa pode atravessar o Pacífico por alguns centavos.

segments.src: You'll also hear **FCL** (full container load — you rent the whole box) versus **LCL** (less than container load — your pallets share a box with other shippers' cargo).
segments.tr: Você também ouvirá **FCL** (carga de contêiner completo — você aluga a caixa inteira) versus **LCL** (menos que uma carga de contêiner — seus paletes compartilham uma caixa com a carga de outros embarcadores).

segments.src: FCL is cheaper per unit if you can fill it; LCL is how smaller businesses get in the game.
segments.tr: FCL é mais barato por unidade se você puder enchê-lo; LCL é como empresas menores entram no jogo.

segments.src: **The freight forwarder** is who ties it together.
segments.tr: **O agente de carga (freight forwarder)** é quem une tudo.

segments.src: A forwarder doesn't usually own ships or planes.
segments.tr: Um agente de carga geralmente não possui navios ou aviões.

segments.src: It books space, consolidates smaller shipments, prepares the paperwork, arranges customs clearance, and manages the handoffs.
segments.tr: Ele reserva espaço, consolida remessas menores, prepara a papelada, organiza o desembaraço aduaneiro e gerencia as transferências.

segments.src: Think of it as a travel agent for cargo — except the itinerary involves customs bonds, a bill of lading, and a truck driver in New Jersey.
segments.tr: Pense nele como um agente de viagens para carga — exceto que o itinerário envolve fianças alfandegárias, um conhecimento de embarque (bill of lading) e um caminhoneiro em New Jersey.

segments.src: One more concept worth knowing: **Incoterms**, the standardized three-letter trade terms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, and others) published by the International Chamber of Commerce.
segments.tr: Mais um conceito que vale a pena conhecer: **Incoterms**, os termos comerciais padronizados de três letras (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP e outros) publicados pela Câmara de Comércio Internacional.

segments.src: They define exactly where the seller's responsibility ends and the buyer's begins — who pays the freight, who carries the risk if the box goes overboard.
segments.tr: Eles definem exatamente onde termina a responsabilidade do vendedor e começa a do comprador — quem paga o frete, quem assume o risco se a caixa cair no mar.

segments.src: "FOB Shanghai" isn't jargon for its own sake; it's a precise allocation of cost and risk, and misreading it is how importers get surprise bills.
segments.tr: "FOB Shanghai" não é jargão por si só; é uma alocação precisa de custo e risco, e interpretá-lo mal é como os importadores recebem contas surpresa.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumo em três linhas

segments.src: 1. Ocean freight moves the overwhelming majority of world trade by volume because it's cheap per ton-mile; air freight moves a small share by weight but a large share by value, buying speed at roughly 10–20x the cost.
segments.tr: 1. O frete marítimo movimenta a esmagadora maioria do comércio mundial em volume porque é barato por tonelada-milha; o frete aéreo movimenta uma pequena parcela por peso, mas uma grande parcela por valor, comprando velocidade a aproximadamente 10–20x o custo.

segments.src: 2. The standardized container (counted in TEU) made global trade cheap by letting one sealed box move across truck, ship, and rail without ever being unpacked.
segments.tr: 2. O contêiner padronizado (contado em TEU) tornou o comércio global barato ao permitir que uma caixa selada se movesse por caminhão, navio e trem sem nunca ser desempacotada.

segments.src: 3. Freight forwarders orchestrate the whole chain — booking, consolidating, clearing customs — while Incoterms define exactly where the seller's risk and cost end and the buyer's begin.

segments.src: > International logistics is the business of moving goods across borders — mostly by ocean (cheap and slow), sometimes by air (fast and expensive), almost always inside a standardized container, and usually arranged by a middleman called a freight forwarder.
segments.tr: > Logistik internasional adalah bisnis pemindahan barang lintas batas — sebagian besar melalui laut (murah dan lambat), terkadang melalui udara (cepat dan mahal), hampir selalu di dalam wadah standar, dan biasanya diatur oleh perantara yang disebut pengiriman barang.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Look around the room you're in.
segments.tr: Lihatlah sekeliling ruangan tempat Anda berada.

segments.src: The laptop, the coffee mug, the sneakers by the door, the lithium cells in your earbuds — odds are most of it crossed an ocean before it reached you.
segments.tr: Laptop, cangkir kopi, sepatu kets di dekat pintu, sel litium di earphone Anda — kemungkinan besar sebagian besar di antaranya melintasi samudra sebelum sampai ke Anda.

segments.src: The question international logistics answers is deceptively simple: **how do you get a thing made in one country into the hands of someone in another, at a cost that still leaves room for profit?**
segments.tr: Pertanyaan yang dijawab oleh logistik internasional sangat sederhana: **bagaimana cara Anda mengirimkan barang yang dibuat di satu negara ke tangan seseorang di negara lain, dengan biaya yang masih menyisakan ruang untuk keuntungan?**

segments.tr: Empat bagian melakukan sebagian besar pekerjaan.

segments.src: **Ocean freight** is the backbone.
segments.tr: **Angkutan laut** adalah tulang punggung.

segments.tr: Kira-kira 80% perdagangan barang dunia berdasarkan volume berjalan melalui laut, karena kapal sangat efisien per ton-mil.

segments.src: 3. Freight forwarders orchestrate the whole chain — booking, consolidating, clearing customs — while Incoterms define exactly where the seller's risk and cost end and the buyer's begin.

ja.title: [Logistics 101 #12] ほぼすべての持ち物を運ぶ40フィートのボックス

segments.src: > International logistics is the business of moving goods across borders — mostly by ocean (cheap and slow), sometimes by air (fast and expensive), almost always inside a standardized container, and usually arranged by a middleman called a freight forwarder.
segments.tr: > 国際物流とは、国境を越えて商品を移動させるビジネスであり、その大部分は海上輸送（安価で遅い）、一部は航空輸送（高速で高価）で行われ、ほぼ常に標準化されたコンテナの内部に収められ、通常はフォワーダーと呼ばれる仲介業者によって手配されます。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 本日のコンセプト

segments.src: Look around the room you're in.
segments.tr: あなたが今いる部屋を見回してください。

segments.src: The laptop, the coffee mug, the sneakers by the door, the lithium cells in your earbuds — odds are most of it crossed an ocean before it reached you.
segments.tr: ラップトップ、コーヒーマグ、ドアのそばのスニーカー、イヤホンのリチウム電池――その大部分は、あなたの元に届くまでに海を渡ってきた可能性が高いでしょう。

segments.src: The question international logistics answers is deceptively simple: **how do you get a thing made in one country into the hands of someone in another, at a cost that still leaves room for profit?**
segments.tr: 国際物流が答える疑問は、一見すると非常にシンプルです：**ある国で作られた商品を、利益を生み出す余地を残したコストで、別の国にいる人の手にどうやって届けるか？**

segments.src: Four pieces do most of the work.
segments.tr: 4つの要素が仕事の大部分を担っています。

segments.src: **Ocean freight** is the backbone.
segments.tr: **海上輸送**はその背骨です。

segments.src: Roughly 80% of world merchandise trade by volume travels by sea, because ships are absurdly efficient per ton-mile.
segments.tr: 世界の物品貿易の容積ベースの約80%が海路で輸送されています。これは、船舶がトンマイルあたりの効率が圧倒的に優れているためです。

segments.src: The tradeoff is time: Shanghai to Los Angeles runs about 14–18 days on the water, and Shanghai to New York (via Panama) closer to 30.
segments.tr: その代償は時間です。上海からロサンゼルスまでは海上でおよそ14〜18日、上海からニューヨーク（パナマ経由）までは30日近くなります。

segments.src: Add port handling, customs, and inland trucking, and a realistic door-to-door number is often 30–45 days.
segments.tr: 港湾荷役、通関、内陸トラック輸送を加えると、現実的なドア・ツー・ドアの期間はしばしば30〜45日になります。

segments.src: **Air freight** flips the equation.
segments.tr: **航空輸送**はその方程式を覆します。

segments.src: Los Angeles to Frankfurt in a day or two, but at a cost that's commonly 10–20x ocean on a per-kilogram basis.
segments.tr: ロサンゼルスからフランクフルトまで1、2日で届きますが、そのコストはキログラム換算で海上輸送の通常10〜20倍になります。

segments.src: So air gets reserved for goods where speed pays for itself: pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, fresh flowers, emergency spare parts, and the fashion item that has to hit stores before the season turns.
segments.tr: そのため航空便は、スピードにコストをかける価値がある商品、すなわち医薬品、半導体、生花、緊急のスペアパーツ、そして季節が変わる前に店頭に並べなければならないファッションアイテムなどのために確保されます。

segments.src: Only a small slice of trade by weight moves by air — but it's a much larger slice by *value*.
segments.tr: 重量ベースでの貿易のほんの一握りしか航空便で移動しませんが、*価値*ベースでははるかに大きな割合を占めます。

segments.src: **The container** is the quiet hero.
segments.tr: **コンテナ**は静かなる英雄です。

segments.src: Before Malcom McLean's standardized steel box debuted in 1956, cargo was loaded piece by piece by longshoremen — slow, theft-prone, and expensive.
segments.tr: マルコム・マクリーンによる標準化されたスチール製ボックスが1956年に登場する前、貨物は港湾労働者によって一つずつ積み下ろされていました――それは遅く、盗難に遭いやすく、高価でした。

segments.src: Today the standard units are the **20-foot** and **40-foot** container, and industry volumes are counted in **TEU** (twenty-foot equivalent unit; one 40-footer = 2 TEU).
segments.tr: 今日、標準的な単位は**20フィート**および**40フィート**コンテナであり、業界の取扱量は**TEU**（20フィート換算単位。1つの40フィートコンテナ = 2 TEU）で数えられます。

segments.src: The box's real magic is that it's *intermodal*: the same sealed unit moves from factory to truck to ship to rail to warehouse without anyone opening it.
segments.tr: このボックスの本当の魔法は、それが*インターモーダル*である点です。同じ密閉されたユニットが、誰も中を開けることなく、工場からトラック、船、鉄道、倉庫へと移動します。

segments.src: That interchangeability is why a shirt can cross the Pacific for a few cents.
segments.tr: その互換性こそが、シャツがわずか数セントで太平洋を渡れる理由です。

segments.src: You'll also hear **FCL** (full container load — you rent the whole box) versus **LCL** (less than container load — your pallets share a box with other shippers' cargo).
segments.tr: また、**FCL**（フル・コンテナ・ロード――ボックス全体を借り切る）と**LCL**（レス・ザン・コンテナ・ロード――あなたのパレットが他の荷主の貨物とボックスを共有する）についても耳にするでしょう。

segments.src: FCL is cheaper per unit if you can fill it; LCL is how smaller businesses get in the game.
segments.tr: FCLは埋めることができれば1単位あたりのコストが安くなり、LCLは中小企業がビジネスに参加する方法です。

segments.src: **The freight forwarder** is who ties it together.
segments.tr: **フォワーダー（貨物利用運送事業者）**は、それらを結びつける存在です。

segments.src: A forwarder doesn't usually own ships or planes.
segments.tr: フォワーダーは通常、船舶や航空機を所有していません。

segments.src: It books space, consolidates smaller shipments, prepares the paperwork, arranges customs clearance, and manages the handoffs.
segments.tr: スペースを予約し、小口貨物を集約し、書類を準備し、通関手続きを手配し、引き継ぎを管理します。

segments.src: Think of it as a travel agent for cargo — except the itinerary involves customs bonds, a bill of lading, and a truck driver in New Jersey.
segments.tr: 貨物のための旅行代理店のようなものと考えてください――ただし、その旅程には税関ボンド、船荷証券、そしてニュージャージーのトラック運転手が含まれています。

segments.src: One more concept worth knowing: **Incoterms**, the standardized three-letter trade terms (EXW, FOB, CIF, DDP, and others) published by the International Chamber of Commerce.
segments.tr: 知っておくべきもう一つのコンセプトは**インコタームズ（貿易条件）**です。これは国際商業会議所（ICC）が発行する標準化された3文字の貿易用語（EXW、FOB、CIF、DDPなど）です。

segments.src: They define exactly where the seller's responsibility ends and the buyer's begins — who pays the freight, who carries the risk if the box goes overboard.
segments.tr: これらは、売り手の責任がどこで終わり、買い手の責任がどこで始まるかを正確に定義します――誰が運賃を支払い、ボックスが海に落下した場合に誰がリスクを負うかなどです。

segments.src: "FOB Shanghai" isn't jargon for its own sake; it's a precise allocation of cost and risk, and misreading it is how importers get surprise bills.
segments.tr: 「FOB上海」は単なる専門用語ではありません。それはコストとリスクの正確な配分であり、これを読み違えると、輸入者は予期せぬ請求を受けることになります。

segments.tr: ## 日常生活において

segments.tr: シューズはベトナム製です。

segments.src: The retailer's freight forwarder books space on a vessel out of Ho Chi Minh City.
segments.tr: 小売業者のフォワーダーは、ホーチミン市発の船舶のスペースを予約します。

segments.src: The shoes — along with about 6,000 other pairs — go into a single 40-foot container, which the retailer has filled as FCL.
segments.tr: シューズは、約6,000足の他のシューズとともに、単一の40フィートコンテナに詰められます。これは小売業者がFCLとして満たしたものです。

segments.src: That box crosses the Pacific in roughly two to three weeks and is craned off at the Port of Los Angeles or Long Beach, which together handle the largest container volumes in the United States.
segments.tr: そのボックスはおよそ2〜3週間で太平洋を横断し、ロサンゼルス港またはロングビーチ港でクレーンで荷下ろしされます。これらは米国最大のコンテナ取扱量を誇ります。

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: **the ocean leg is often one of the cheapest lines on the invoice.** Trans-Pacific container rates swing wildly with market conditions — they spiked to extraordinary levels during the 2021 supply chain crunch and fell hard afterward — but spread across thousands of pairs, the per-shoe ocean cost typically lands in the range of pennies to a couple of dollars.
segments.tr: 人々を驚かせるのはこの部分です：**海上区間は請求書の中で最も安い項目の一つであることがよくあります。** 太平洋横断コンテナの運賃は市場状況によって激しく変動します――2021年のサプライチェーンの混乱時には異常な水準まで高騰し、その後急落しました――しかし、数千足に分散させると、シューズ1足あたりの海上コストは通常ペニー（数セント）から数ドルの範囲に収まります。
